title: Xanthe and the Gravity
premise: Tamsin Montrose is the last active terraformer aboard the seed-ship Halcyon Verge, tending an atmosphere garden for colonists who won't wake for another century. When she finds her own mother's name—long listed as dead—on the manifest of a shuttle that never launched, she uncovers a fleet-wide conspiracy: two cryo-banks, one powered by stolen truce energy, and only enough resources to wake half of humanity. As the fleet's fragile truce expires and factions move to seize the banks, Tamsin must choose between waking the loyalists who abandoned her family or the dissidents who might forgive nothing. She ends the cycle by refusing both lists, waking instead the children born in transit—the found family no faction counted—and seeding a new world with the garden meant for people not yet born.
about_author: Casper Coldharbour is the pen name of a former hydrologist who spent six years on Antarctic ice-core crews before turning to fiction. They write slow-burn science fiction about people who maintain things nobody thanks them for.

chapters.title: The Garden of Unborn Weather
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She walks the terraforming decks at shift's end, logging humidity, soil microbes, and the silence of a ship built for ten thousand sleepers. Establishes her ritual care and isolation; the emotional beat is tender loneliness disguised as competence.

chapters.title: Manifest 114
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Auditing old cargo records, she finds a shuttle listed as never flown—with her mother Ilsa Montrose's name among its passengers, dated three years after Ilsa's official death. The beat is a cold spike of disbelief.

chapters.title: What the Dead Owe the Logs
chapters.summary: Tamsin confronts Archivist Pell, the aging keeper of fleet records, who stonewalls her with bureaucratic warmth. She notices his hands shake when she says 'Montrose.' Beat: suspicion taking root.

chapters.title: Voices from the Cold Bank
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, night shift. She descends toward Cryo-Bank A against regulations and hears maintenance drones servicing a bank officially decommissioned. Someone is keeping it alive. Beat: dread mixed with exhilaration.

chapters.title: The Man Who Repairs Ghosts
chapters.summary: Introduce Dev Okonkwo, a disgraced engineer working off-books to keep Bank A running. He catches Tamsin snooping; instead of reporting her, he asks what she knows about her mother. Beat: wary alliance.

chapters.title: Two Banks, One Sun
chapters.summary: Dev explains the split: Bank A holds dissidents and transit-born children, Bank B the loyalist elite—and the power draw sustaining A was siphoned during the truce negotiations decades ago. If discovered, it means civil war. Beat: the scale of the secret lands.

chapters.title: Ilsa Montrose, Passenger
chapters.summary: Through recovered letters, Tamsin learns her mother faked her death to smuggle dissident families into Bank A—including Tamsin herself, as an infant, before being reassigned to Bank B by faction politics. Beat: grief reframed as inheritance.

chapters.title: The Truce Clock
chapters.summary: Council POV (Commander Reyes). The fleet's resource-sharing truce expires in fourteen months; Reyes knows the power ledger doesn't balance and quietly orders an audit. Beat: the hunters begin moving.

chapters.title: Small Treasons
chapters.summary: Tamsin falsifies garden output reports to mask Bank A's energy signature, using her terraformer credentials for the first time as a weapon. Beat: guilt braided with purpose—she has become her mother.

chapters.title: The Children Who Were Never Counted
chapters.summary: Dev shows Tamsin the manifest anomaly: forty-one children born in transit, legally nonexistent, distributed between banks. One name matches a gardener's apprentice she's mentored for years: Junie. Beat: personal stakes detonate.

chapters.title: Junie
chapters.summary: Junie's POV. The apprentice reveals she's always known she had no birth record, and that someone named Ilsa paid for her pod. She begs Tamsin not to make her a cause. Beat: found family asserted against Tamsin's crusade.

chapters.title: Reyes Closes In
chapters.summary: Reyes' audit flags the siphon. An investigator, Sef Adisa, arrives on the Halcyon Verge—charming, thorough, and assigned to find where the missing terawatts went. Beat: the walls tighten.

chapters.title: Dinner with the Auditor
chapters.summary: Tamsin hosts Sef under pretense of touring the gardens, testing how much he knows. He quotes her own falsified report back to her, smiling. Beat: cat-and-mouse flirtation with menace underneath.

chapters.title: What Loyalty Costs
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter—Ilsa's POV, thirty years prior. Ilsa chooses to fake her death, leaving toddler Tamsin behind because a Montrose on the loyalist rolls would protect the hidden children. Beat: the mother's sacrifice made legible and unbearable.

chapters.title: Bank B Wakes Early
chapters.summary: Reyes secretly begins thawing loyalist cadres ahead of the truce expiry, citing 'contingency readiness.' Dev intercepts the power surge; Bank A will brown out within weeks. Beat: countdown starts.

chapters.title: The Bargain at Airlock Nine
chapters.summary: Sef corners Tamsin: he knows about the siphon and offers to bury it if she helps him expose Reyes instead—he has his own grudge against the command clique. Beat: uneasy triangulation; trust extended cautiously.

chapters.title: Garden War
chapters.summary: Tamsin reroutes the garden's photosynthetic grid to feed Bank A, risking the unborn colony's atmosphere timeline. Junie catches her and, furious, threatens to report her. Beat: love against duty turns inward.

chapters.title: The Ledger of Small Mercies
chapters.summary: Pell, dying, gives Tamsin his master archive: proof Reyes ordered the original theft of Bank A's endowment, and Ilsa's final letter addressed to Tamsin, unopened for thirty years. Beat: inheritance delivered.

chapters.title: My Mother's Handwriting
chapters.summary: Tamsin reads the letter alone in the garden: Ilsa writes that she chose the invisible work—tending, hiding, feeding—because 'someone must grow the weather for people who can't yet vote.' Beat: catharsis; Tamsin stops resenting her mother's absence.

chapters.title: Junie's Choice
chapters.summary: Junie, having read the manifests herself, comes back—not to forgive but to enlist. If the children are pawns, they'll become players. Beat: reconciliation through shared agency rather than sentiment.

chapters.title: Midpoint: The Fleet Votes
chapters.summary: Multi-POV interlude. The Council convenes on truce renewal; Reyes proposes 'staged awakening'—her bank first, the rest 'as resources allow.' The motion passes. Beat: the legal machinery of injustice clicks forward.

chapters.title: Sabotage or Salvation
chapters.summary: Dev proposes physically severing Bank B's priority feed—an act the fleet will call terrorism. Sef warns them Reyes wants exactly this pretext. Beat: the plan fractures the alliance; Tamsin must decide what she's willing to be.

chapters.title: The Invisible Fleet
chapters.summary: Junie discovers the transit-born children were seeded across all ships as insurance—a network of unrecorded people who could, coordinated, control every airlock and comm relay. Beat: hope arrives disguised as an accident of history.

chapters.title: Counting the Uncounted
chapters.summary: Tamsin broadcasts on an old gardening channel, using Ilsa's childhood cipher, calling the unregistered to stand up. Replies arrive from nine ships over one long night. Beat: awe; loneliness ends.

chapters.title: Reyes Learns the Garden's Name
chapters.summary: Reyes traces the broadcast to the Halcyon Verge and orders Sef to arrest the 'sabotage cell.' Sef stalls, buying three days, revealing his hand to Tamsin fully. Beat: loyalty shifts; the auditor becomes conspirator.

chapters.title: Brownout
chapters.summary: Bank A's power fails during a storm-cycle; pods begin warming. Dev and Tamsin race through flooded corridors to patch the feed while Junie organizes the awakened children to manually circulate coolant. Beat: white-knuckle action; found family forged in crisis.

chapters.title: First Faces
chapters.summary: Eleven pods open early—among them a woman who knew Ilsa, who tells Tamsin her mother survived the fake death by four years and spent them teaching the transit-born to read the stars. Beat: grief and gift entwined.

chapters.title: The Arrest of Dev Okonkwo
chapters.summary: Reyes' marines take Dev during the repair aftermath. Tamsin, hidden, watches and does nothing—surviving to fight. Beat: shame; the cost of strategy over heart.

chapters.title: Trial as Theater
chapters.summary: Dev is publicly charged with energy piracy. His testimony becomes a platform: he names the siphon, the two banks, the forty-one children, on open fleet comms before they cut his mic. Beat: defiance; the secret dies loudly.

chapters.title: The Fleet Holds Its Breath
chapters.summary: Multi-POV. Ships declare for Bank A, Bank B, or neutrality; skirmishes flare at junction points. Tamsin realizes the war everyone feared is arriving anyway—but now the uncounted hold the infrastructure. Beat: chaos with leverage.

chapters.title: Negotiating with the Enemy of My Mother
chapters.summary: Tamsin requests parley with Reyes, presenting Pell's ledger proving Reyes stole the endowment. Reyes, cornered, offers Tamsin everything—except the children's independence. Beat: temptation of a clean deal that requires betrayal.

chapters.title: Refusal
chapters.summary: Tamsin declines on open channel: 'You don't get to inherit my mother's crime by purchasing mine.' The fleet hears. Reyes orders the Verge seized. Beat: point of no return; duty redefined.

chapters.title: The Siege of the Gardens
chapters.summary: Marines board the Verge; Tamsin, Junie, and the network turn the terraforming systems themselves into defenses—atmosphere locks, fog banks, pollen storms. Beat: the gardener's knowledge as warfare; triumphant ingenuity.

chapters.title: Sef's Price
chapters.summary: Sef defects openly, delivering Reyes' private orders as evidence, but is shot covering the retreat to the deep banks. Beat: sacrifice; the auditor pays for his late conscience.

chapters.title: Climax: The Truce Expires
chapters.summary: With weapons armed fleet-wide and the truce clock hitting zero, Tamsin seizes the central comm and makes her move: she wakes neither list. She opens every transit-born child's pod across all eleven ships simultaneously. Beat: the fulcrum of the whole book—one act that belongs to no faction.

chapters.title: The Vote That Wasn't Scheduled
chapters.summary: The newly woken, unaligned generation—hundreds strong, holding airlocks, relays, and the Verge's garden—demand a new tally: not which half wakes first, but on what terms anyone wakes. Reyes' coalition splinters. Beat: power inverted without a massacre.

chapters.title: Terms of Thaw
chapters.summary: Negotiations: staged awakening continues under joint stewardship, Dev freed to oversee the banks, Reyes retired to face a truth commission rather than a firing squad. Beat: exhausted, hard-won compromise that honors neither side's pride.

chapters.title: What We Plant in Ruins
chapters.summary: Tamsin returns to the garden, now scorched from the siege, and begins replanting with seeds Ilsa hoarded. Junie works beside her; Dev brings Bank A's first healthy sleepers to visit the green. Beat: quiet repair; love persisted through duty.

chapters.title: Descent
chapters.summary: Eighteen months later, the fleet reaches the target world. The first landers carry the transit-born, the garden's seed stock, and Ilsa's letters. Tamsin watches the atmosphere thicken over raw ground—weather being born. Beat: fulfillment of the title promise.

chapters.title: Xanthe
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Tamsin's POV. The colony names itself Xanthe—for the golden light of its new dawn—and raises a marker listing the uncounted first. Tamsin logs one last entry: the garden is no longer for people not yet born. Beat: inheritance completed; the invisible made foundational.
